clue.text: Against new annexe with liquor, when we all have twelve-hour day

definitions.text: when we all have twelve-hour day

indicators.note: something new has been made over, so the following words are to be rebuilt in a fresh order

blocks.note: V, short for versus, means against
taken as written, as fodder
taken as written, as fodder

explanation.surface: A drinker sets an extra room with liquor against the long days of the year.
explanation.walkthrough: The twelve letters of annexe and liquor are rearranged together after the V.
explanation.definitionFit: At the spring equinox, around 20 March, daylight and darkness each last roughly twelve hours across the whole globe.

clue.text: People's party secures right for one over eighteen, perhaps

indicators.note: to secure something is to hold it fast inside, so one piece is wrapped round another

blocks.note: vulgar originally meant of the common people
a faction is a party within a larger group
R is the usual abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A populist party locks in the right to serve someone over eighteen, as at a bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One over eighteen' looks like an adult of drinking age; it is the fraction 1/18.
explanation.definitionFit: A common fraction written as numerator above denominator, like 1/18, is called a vulgar fraction, as opposed to a decimal.

clue.text: It may spur plasterer with shortage of time

indicators.note: a shortage means something is missing, so a letter has to be removed

blocks.note: a trowel is the plasterer's tool, the thing that does the plastering
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Something may goad a plasterer who is running out of time.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the T from TROWEL to leave ROWEL.
explanation.definitionFit: A rowel is the spiked revolving wheel at the end of a rider's spur; the clue's 'It may spur' is a cryptic way of saying it pricks a horse.

clue.text: One German's agreed to infiltrate a brazen revolution in part of Iran

indicators.note: a revolution overturns the existing order, so the words before it are scrambled
to infiltrate is to get inside, so the first pieces go into the middle of the other

blocks.note: the Roman numeral for one
ja is German for yes, the German's agreement
taken as written, as fodder

explanation.surface: A lone German agrees to infiltrate a bold uprising somewhere in Iran.
explanation.walkthrough: IJA goes inside AZERBAN, the shuffled letters of a brazen, between its sixth and seventh letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Azerbaijan is the name of the northwestern region of Iran, home to many Azeris, as well as of the neighbouring republic.

clue.text: Outstanding issue incorporating new printing measure

indicators.note: to incorporate is to take into the body, so the outer word holds the others inside

blocks.note: to emit is to issue or send out
N is the abbreviation for new
an en is a printer's unit of width, half an em

explanation.surface: An unpaid magazine issue is held up over a typographical measurement.
explanation.walkthrough: Printers measure type width in ems and ens; an en is half an em, roughly the width of a letter n.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone eminent stands out above others in rank or reputation, which is the figurative sense of outstanding.

clue.text: Get a French dress or shift out of the cloth

blocks.note: un is French for a
a frock is a dress

explanation.surface: Buy a French dress, or else a shift, the clothing kind.
explanation.walkthrough: Dress and shift look like garments; 'the cloth' is the clergy, and shift means remove.
explanation.definitionFit: To unfrock a priest is to strip them of clerical office, expelling them from the clergy, which is called the cloth.

clue.text: Half normal? Not in dialect

indicators.note: half of a six-letter word is its first three letters, so only those are kept

blocks.note: the first half of the word normal
N stands for no or not, as on a yes/no form

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether half of something is normal and is told it is not, in local speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Norn is the extinct Scandinavian language once spoken in Orkney and Shetland, surviving in words of the local dialect.

clue.text: Nagging wife disturbed Texan inhaling joint quietly

indicators.note: disturbed means thrown into disorder, so the word's letters are jumbled
inhaling draws something in, so the scrambled word swallows the next pieces

blocks.note: taken as written, as fodder
the hip is a joint of the body
p, piano, is the musical direction for quietly

explanation.surface: A henpecked Texan's wife scolds him as he quietly smokes a joint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joint' suggests cannabis, which suits inhaling, but it is the hip.
explanation.definitionFit: Xanthippe, Socrates's wife, became a byword for a shrewish, scolding woman, so her name stands for any nagging wife.

clue.text: Usual choice of outdoor venues

blocks.note: first meaning: ordinary, everyday
second meaning: read literally, an either-or between two open-air places

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase read word by word offers a pick between a common, a public green, and a garden.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes something ordinary and unremarkable, the run-of-the-mill sort, which is what usual means here.

clue.text: Outstanding artwork in blue, needing replacement

blocks.note: feeling blue is feeling low
a relief is someone who takes over from another, a replacement

explanation.surface: A fine painting done in blue needs to be restored or swapped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outstanding' is literal: the carving stands out from its background.
explanation.definitionFit: Low relief, or bas-relief, is sculpture whose figures project slightly from a flat surface, so it physically stands out.

clue.text: Fiddler finally playing the same music

indicators.note: finally points to the end of the word, so only its closing letter is kept

blocks.note: the final letter of Fiddler
a show that is on is playing
do, short for ditto, means the same

explanation.surface: A violinist ends up playing the same tune over again.
explanation.definitionFit: A rondo is a musical form in which a main theme keeps returning between contrasting episodes.

clue.text: One isn't prepared to address the House

definitions.text: One isn't prepared to address the House

blocks.clueFragment: One isn't prepared to address the House
blocks.note: surface reading: a backbencher who is not ready to give a speech in Parliament
setter's reading: the speech itself is improvised, made up on the spot without a script

explanation.walkthrough: It sounds like an MP who has failed to prepare; the answer is the unrehearsed speech such a speaker gives.
explanation.definitionFit: An off-the-cuff remark is spoken without preparation, so it is the thing that is not prepared before addressing listeners.

clue.text: Returning to the old part of Chiswick

indicators.note: returning means going back the way you came, so the words are read backwards

blocks.note: taken as written
ye is the old form of the, as in Ye Olde Tea Shoppe

explanation.surface: Someone goes back to the historic quarter of a West London district.
explanation.walkthrough: Chiswick is a district of West London on the Thames, and Chiswick Eyot is a small island in the river there.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyot is a small river island, and Chiswick Eyot is one such island belonging to that stretch of the Thames.

clue.text: Comic sound effect enhancing hit production

definitions.text: Comic sound effect enhancing hit production

blocks.clueFragment: Comic sound effect enhancing hit production
blocks.note: surface reading: a funny noise added to boost a chart-topping record
setter's reading: in a comic strip, the word printed beside a punch to make the blow louder on the page

explanation.walkthrough: 'Comic' and 'hit production' suggest pop music; the comic is a cartoon strip and the hit a punch.
explanation.definitionFit: Comic books print onomatopoeic words such as this one alongside a punch or crash to convey the noise of impact.

clue.text: The Diet of Worms?

blocks.note: surface reading: the 1521 imperial assembly at Worms where Luther was condemned
setter's reading: food made of things that look like worms

explanation.walkthrough: A diet was an assembly of the Holy Roman Empire and Worms is a German city; here diet means food and worms are wriggling creatures.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian name of this very thin pasta literally means little worms, so eating it is a meal of worms.

clue.text: One may profit from getting 18 out of bed

definitions.text: One may profit from getting 18 out of bed

blocks.clueFragment: One may profit from getting 18 out of bed
blocks.note: surface reading: someone who makes money rousing sleepers who are always lying in
setter's reading: 18 is the answer to 18 across, plants that flower for one season, lifted from a flower bed for sale

explanation.walkthrough: 'Out of bed' suggests waking people; the bed is a flower bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A shopkeeper who sells cut flowers and bedding plants earns a living from blooms grown in beds.

clue.text: Offensive broadcast on box - promises to make amends

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, as seed is, so the letters are strewn into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, as fodder
IOUs are written promises to repay a debt

explanation.surface: A rude television programme ends with the broadcaster promising to apologise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Box' and 'broadcast' suggest television; box here is just letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Obnoxious and offensive are synonyms, both describing behaviour that is extremely unpleasant and objectionable to others.

clue.text: Nitrogen put in to preserve an item of bone structure

indicators.note: something put in to another is placed inside it

blocks.note: to keep food is to preserve it
N is the chemical symbol for nitrogen
taken as written

explanation.surface: Nitrogen is added as a preservative to part of a skeleton.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Preserve' reads as the chemistry of food storage, but it is simply a verb meaning retain.
explanation.definitionFit: The kneepan is an old name for the kneecap or patella, one of the bones of the human skeleton.

clue.text: Origin of Union given in history books

indicators.note: the origin of a word is where it starts, so only its opening letter is used
given in means placed inside, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: the first letter of Union
annals are historical records kept year by year

explanation.surface: The founding of a union is recorded in history books.
explanation.walkthrough: U goes inside ANNALS after its fourth letter. Children's annuals are hardback yearly books, a British Christmas tradition.
explanation.definitionFit: An annual is a book published once a year, such as a yearbook or a children's compilation.

clue.text: Just a taste of the French course to study

definitions.text: Just a taste of the French
definitions.note: the answer is a French word, hence of the French

blocks.note: soup is a course of a meal
to con is to study carefully, as a text

explanation.surface: A diner samples French cuisine and then reads up on it.
explanation.walkthrough: Course looks like an academic course to go with study; here it is part of a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: A soupçon is a tiny amount or hint, borrowed from French where it literally means suspicion.

clue.text: Turned in creep mocking an equal

indicators.note: in tells us the letters lie inside the words that follow
turned means facing the other way, so the run of letters is read backwards

blocks.note: a run of letters inside these words, read from right to left

explanation.surface: A sycophant is mocked as an equal.
explanation.walkthrough: Reading creep mocking backwards gives gnikcompeerc, with the answer inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A compeer is a person of equal standing or rank, a peer or companion, an old literary word.

clue.text: Article put in as a mathematical section of standard texts

indicators.note: put in means inserted, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: an is the indefinite article
a conic is a conic section, the curve made when a plane cuts a cone

explanation.surface: An article appears in a maths section of the standard textbooks.
explanation.walkthrough: A conic section is the curve cut from a cone by a plane: circle, ellipse, parabola or hyperbola.
explanation.definitionFit: Canonic means belonging to the canon, the accepted body of authoritative scriptures or works.

clue.text: One should follow audible directions

blocks.note: surface reading: someone who ought to obey instructions they can hear
setter's reading: a cab driven where the passenger tells the driver to go

explanation.walkthrough: It looks like a person told what to do; the one obeying spoken instructions is a vehicle for hire.
explanation.definitionFit: A hired cab goes wherever the passenger tells the driver, following the route called out from the back seat.

clue.text: Like a horse that's neither first nor last - one of several arriving together

indicators.note: dropping both the first and the last means losing the word's two ends

blocks.note: equine means like or relating to a horse

explanation.surface: A racehorse finishes neither first nor last in a bunched field.
explanation.walkthrough: Strip both ends from EQUINE.
explanation.definitionFit: A quin, short for quintuplet, is one of five babies born at the same birth, so they arrive together.

clue.text: Reptile and bird portrayed by artist

blocks.note: a cob is a male swan
RA, Royal Academician, is the usual abbreviation for artist

explanation.surface: A painter depicts a snake and a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The cobra is a venomous snake, and snakes are reptiles.

clue.text: Airline has equipment done up to colourful design

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means read from the bottom, so the word is written backwards

blocks.note: BA is British Airways
kit is equipment

explanation.surface: An airline's gear is smartened up with a bright pattern.
explanation.definitionFit: Batik is a method of dyeing cloth using wax to resist the dye, producing vivid patterned fabric.

clue.text: Ridicule disheartened Yorick

indicators.note: losing heart means losing the middle, so the central letters are removed

blocks.note: Yorick was the king's jester whose skull Hamlet holds

explanation.surface: Mocking a downcast Yorick.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the middle ST out of JESTER. Hamlet's 'Alas, poor Yorick' speech remembers him as a fellow of infinite jest.
explanation.definitionFit: To jeer is to mock or deride someone with taunts, so the verb is a synonym of ridicule.

clue.text: Love the area - it's bracing

blocks.note: love is zero in tennis, which looks like O
a zone is an area

explanation.surface: Someone declares their love for a place with fresh, invigorating air.
explanation.walkthrough: In British usage ozone is the fresh air of the seaside, popularly thought to be invigorating.
explanation.definitionFit: Ozone was the old seaside-resort term for the tangy, refreshing sea air believed to be good for health.

clue.text: Combined texts, for example, in rip-off - not glossy edition

definitions.note: the definition by example: texts are the sort of thing that are combined

blocks.note: a con is a swindle
flat paint or finish is matt rather than glossy
ed. is the abbreviation for edition

explanation.surface: A cheap reissue merges several texts and is printed on matt paper.
explanation.definitionFit: To conflate is to blend two versions of a text into one, so combined texts have been conflated.

clue.text: Help coward to escape - a youngster

blocks.note: with to escape at the end, help means spring, as in spring a prisoner from jail
a chicken is a coward

explanation.surface: Someone helps a timid person break free; the timid one is just a kid.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay reads as a sentence: help a coward to escape.
explanation.definitionFit: A spring chicken is a young person, mostly in the phrase 'no spring chicken' said of someone no longer youthful.
